relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: Preclinical studies show that CGRP released in the dura, trigeminal ganglion, and brainstem promotes the activation of satellite glial cells, the release of nitric oxide and pro-inflammatory cytokines, and the sustained sensitization of peripheral and central trigeminovascular neurons (21).

relationships.subject: CGRP monoclonal antibodies
relationships.evidence_quote: CGRP mAbs prevent the development of activity-induced sensitization of dural-projecting nociceptors and of wide-dynamic-range neurons in the TCC (13).

relationships.subject: guanfacine
relationships.evidence_quote: presynaptic α2-adrenergic receptor activation on trigeminal primary afferents may inhibit voltage-gated calcium influx and consequently suppress the release of CGRP, glutamate, substance P, and nitric oxide

relationships.subject: ADRA2B
relationships.evidence_quote: The missense single-nucleotide variant rs29000569 in the ADRA2B gene showed an association with the Phecode for trigeminal nerve disorders (170 cases, 25,739 controls; odds ratio 4.62, p = 0.003075) (12).

key_findings: Hypothesis article proposing guanfacine (alpha2A agonist) as chronic migraine preventive via presynaptic inhibition of CGRP/glutamate/substance P release, reduced sensitization, and descending inhibition; direct migraine evidence is lacking.
PheWAS links ADRA2B variant rs29000569 to trigeminal nerve disorders; a crossover trial of guanfacine added to lidocaine nerve blocks showed modest analgesia (1.02 NRS difference).
